items.title: Cancel stops calls already in flight

items.title: Registry: labels key on the ADR-0041 frozen snapshot, not the recipe hash alone
items.section: Before the study registry's first entry
items.summary: A label must key on the recipe, the prompt template versions, the models, the engine, the renderer and the fallback policy.
items.trigger: before the study registry's first entry
blockedBy: Pin C1-H's parent hash before Study 1's prompt registration
items.landNowWhy: Its trigger is years away, and the frozen-version snapshot itself is not built.

items.title: Registry: lineage check cross-checks exposure.jsonl against the ledger
items.section: Before the study registry's first entry
items.summary: The lineage check must not trust an exposure.jsonl restored from an older backup. It should cross-check against the ledger's judging calls (exposure.ts in the gateway).
items.trigger: before the study registry's first entry
items.landNowWhy: Its trigger has not fired, and no study writes exposure yet.

items.title: Registry: the review's other activation prerequisites
items.section: Before the study registry's first entry
items.summary: A treatment-fidelity dry run, instrument separation, operational governance and independent metric validation. They restate ADR-0041, 0044, 0052, 0054 and 0055.
items.landNowWhy: These are research-track activation steps for 2027.

items.title: Study engine: halt a run when the served model differs from the profile (§5.1)
items.section: Before the study registry's first entry
items.summary: A protocol requirement that ADR-0102 leaves to the study engine: a run stops when the returned model is not the profile's.
items.trigger: "before the first study run (the pilot or any development-brief tuning)"
blockedBy: First live run with real keys and real money
items.landNowWhy: It needs each provider's live served-model labels (the first live run) and the study engine (the harness).

items.title: Study engine: count a second refusal as Class Q 'provider refusal' (§5.2)
items.section: Before the study registry's first entry
items.summary: Count it from the ledger's declined and retryOf entries and from the model-declined events.
items.landNowWhy: It belongs to the study engine, which is not started.

items.title: Public Program Registry (ADR-0046, CR3) with entries before a study's first paid call
items.section: Before the study registry's first entry
items.summary: The public Program Registry, separate from the product's label registry in registry.ts, gates every study's paid calls through the spend gate. Nothing in the code checks it today.
items.trigger: "CR3 needs Program Registry entries before a study's first paid call"
items.landNowWhy: It needs the public mirror (the owner's step) and the spend gate (the harness).

items.title: Write the research roadmap for the Program Registry
items.section: Before the study registry's first entry
items.summary: Ladder rungs, candidate Paper 2 domains, comparator-selection criteria, and the deferred arms and measures: ADR-0061's GPT worker arm, ADR-0035's deferred ablations and Appendix B.2 item 12. No roadmap exists, though ADR-0061 says the GPT arm is 'logged in the roadmap'.
items.trigger: none stated ("No roadmap has been written")
items.landNowWhy: A draft needs no build, and the red team advised publishing it early. But its home, the public Program Registry, does not exist, and the Paper 2 domains are a research-direction choice for the owner.

items.title: D1 Baseline set
items.summary: Confirm the recommended B-Skill, B-Outside and B-BoN, gated behind H1a. This is the same decision as the playbook's 'Confirm the baseline set'.
items.landNowWhy: The owner's decision. Until then the harness assumes the default.

items.title: D4 Registered Report venue
items.summary: PLOS ONE if it accepts sealed generation before acceptance, otherwise RSOS; stop if neither does. This is the research track's go/no-go.
items.landNowWhy: It needs the editors' written answers, and the repository has no record or draft of the questions being sent. The October 2026 deadline is this month.

items.title: D7 Monitor, deputy, guarantor
items.summary: Three different people fill the Monitor, deputy key-holder and guarantor roles.
items.landNowWhy: It needs people to be found.

items.title: D8 Ethics route and rater population
items.summary: Default: the academic co-investigator's IRB, US and UK raters, disclosure that the pages are AI-generated, and a corporate Prolific account unless an institution pays.
items.landNowWhy: No co-investigator has been found. The IRB target is November 2026.

items.title: D9 Funding, patents, legal entity
items.summary: Who funds Study 1, whether any patent is filed, and the legal entity. This is the same decision as the playbook action.
items.landNowWhy: The owner's decision.

items.title: D10 Ratifications and charter interpretations
items.summary: The ratification pass described in the playbook's 'Ratify the 15 by-continuation ADRs' row.
items.landNowWhy: The owner's review. The CR11 interpretation also needs the Monitor's co-signature.

items.title: D13 Spending ceiling
items.summary: Duplicate of the Pricing row 'Set the Study 1 spending ceiling'.
items.landNowWhy: Its inputs do not exist yet.

items.title: D24 Product consequences ('Worse' rows)
items.summary: Fill in what the product does if a configuration is found Worse. A draft table is in protocol v1.1.
items.landNowWhy: Due before Stage 1 (about April 2027). The CR10 tables are finalized only after D1.

items.title: SEED string source in the product
items.summary: Keep the runner-injected random seed string (crypto.randomBytes) or switch to a model-written one, which D.6 found generally scored higher. Behaviour and recipe hashes stay unchanged until it is decided.
items.landNowWhy: No study or claim about SEED is planned, and changing it would change recipe hashes.

items.title: Judge hosting and data residency; who needs Lab access
items.summary: Choose the Judge app's host (Vercel, Cloudflare, or an EU or UK VPS), with stimuli on a cookieless origin and the validity service on Monitor-controlled infrastructure, and decide who gets Lab access.
items.trigger: "Judge: after D8, before the Judge app is built. Lab: before the Lab is built"
items.landNowWhy: It follows D8, and the Judge app is not started.

items.title: Independent Integrity Monitor
items.summary: Find and contract a paid, independent methodologist. The Monitor holds every study key, alone sees pilot effects, co-signs deviations and runs the confirmatory analysis.
items.landNowWhy: Owner recruitment. The contract needs the legal reviewer, and the venue go/no-go should come first. The ADR index says Claude can draft the search brief and a contract outline once the owner starts.

items.title: Deputy key-holder
items.summary: An independent second key-holder who acts on the scripted Monitor steps if the Monitor is unavailable.
items.landNowWhy: Found together with the Monitor.

items.title: Guarantor
items.summary: A non-conflicted author who signs ICMJE's full-access statement. Must be a different person from the Monitor and the deputy.
items.landNowWhy: Due around 2028.

items.title: Academic co-investigator
items.summary: Provides the IRB route (and Prolific's academic rate if their institution pays). Can be the deputy or the guarantor, not both.
items.landNowWhy: The owner's search. No candidate is recorded.

items.title: Independent copywriter
items.summary: Screens the sampling frame, fictionalizes the briefs and writes the fixed copy decks under a rulebook: 12 development briefs before the pilot and 72 during Stage 1 review.
items.landNowWhy: Owner recruitment. Its target window is now, and no action is recorded.

items.title: Independent designer
items.summary: Picks the critic-calibration exemplars and builds the defect gold pairs and positive-control pairs under preregistered rules.
items.landNowWhy: Recruited through the vendor, which is not yet chosen.

items.title: Second transcriber
items.summary: Someone outside the team who transcribes the article's prompts word for word, independently of the owner. The Monitor can do it once contracted.
items.landNowWhy: A person outside the team must be found (Claude does not count as independent). Due 2026-11-30.

items.title: Outside baseline owner
items.summary: The owner of a competing open-source approach, invited under a registered rule to provide B-Outside.
items.trigger: "Invitations after the Monitor is in post"
items.landNowWhy: Waits for the Monitor.

items.title: Lay raters (Prolific)
items.summary: US and UK desktop participants who judge forced-choice pairs in 30-minute sessions at $15/h.
items.landNowWhy: Needs the IRB and the Judge app.

items.title: Expert designer panel (20)
items.summary: Twenty portfolio-verified designers from outside the team's network, about 3 hours each. They give estimates only.
items.landNowWhy: Needed only in 2027.

items.title: Detector coders (2)
items.summary: Two independent coders label 150 pages to validate the tell detector (kappa of at least .70).
items.landNowWhy: Needed during Stage 1 review in 2027.

items.title: Statistician (optional)
items.summary: Runs the confirmatory analysis if the Monitor contracts one under the same independence test.
items.landNowWhy: Optional, and the Monitor's call.

items.title: Red team (3-5)
items.summary: Paid outside reviewers, at least one from a competing approach, who review the manuscript and the arm-specific code paths.
items.landNowWhy: Due before Stage 1 (about April 2027).

items.title: CODECHECK
items.summary: An independent reproduction of the analysis pipeline, with a certificate that has a DOI.
items.landNowWhy: Due around 2028.

items.title: Legal reviewer
items.summary: Reviews the Monitor contract (the six CR1 powers, results escrow, publication freedom), the publication-freedom clause for every deal, and the licences.
items.landNowWhy: Owner hiring. It sits upstream of the Monitor's mid-November target.

items.title: Recruiting vendor
items.summary: One third-party vendor recruits the experts, the designer, the coders and the Study 1b operators.
items.landNowWhy: Owner hiring, not yet due.

items.title: Study 1b designer-operators (8)
items.summary: Eight operators who run human-in-the-loop C1 under scripted procedures in Study 1b.
blockedBy: C1's other entry routes are not modelled
items.landNowWhy: Study 1b is not designed yet.

items.title: Journal editors
items.summary: The PLOS ONE RR and RSOS editors answer the venue questions that decide the go/no-go.
items.landNowWhy: They can answer only once the questions are sent, and that is not recorded.

items.title: Article author / publisher
items.summary: Confirms the transcribed prompts and permits their publication. Without permission by the freeze, the prompts are registered by hash and shared confidentially.
items.landNowWhy: Waits for the transcription.

items.title: Ask PLOS ONE Registered Reports and Royal Society Open Science the venue questions
items.summary: Ask both venues seven questions in writing: sealed generation before IPA, a successor-model rule, minimum power, the sealed pilot report route, charges, Stage 1 turnaround, and conflict-of-interest terms. If neither accepts sealed generation, stop before any pilot spend.
items.landNowWhy: Nothing blocks it, and its deadline is this month, with no draft or record of sending in the repository. Claude can draft the emails from the playbook's questions, but only the owner sends them, and the owner has put the research track behind live product use.

items.title: Transcribe the article's prompts (B-Random, SEED, critic-loop worker, ASSET)
items.summary: The owner and a second independent transcriber copy the article's prompts verbatim from the live page (the PDF crops words), reconcile the two copies, and ask the author to confirm and permit publication.
items.landNowWhy: The owner's own transcription has no blocker and is due 2026-11-30. The reconciliation needs a second transcriber who has not been found. The protocol still carries its [TRANSCRIBE] markers.

items.title: IRB submission
items.summary: Submit to the co-investigator's IRB, or an independent one, with a consent form that names the commercial sponsor and says the pages were AI-generated.
blockedBy: "Product data never feeds a study" against ADR-0041 rule 3
items.landNowWhy: No co-investigator has been found, and the consent wording waits on the product-data row and the sponsor (D9).

items.title: Anthropic organization account and dedicated study keys
items.summary: An organization account with one workspace per arm, and dedicated spend-capped study keys at every provider (needed for CR7's per-key reconciliation). These are separate from the product's keys.
items.landNowWhy: Research keys are needed only when the cost probe and pilot run, and both wait on the harness.

items.title: Ask providers for higher rate and spend limits
items.summary: Raise the provider tiers ahead of confirmatory generation (about $15k to $20k in about 10 days, bursty). New organizations start in low tiers.
items.landNowWhy: Due around mid-2027.

items.title: Public record for the charter (public mirror, DOI snapshots, signed commits)
items.summary: A public mirror of the research ADRs, the Program Registry and the deviation log, DOI snapshots at milestones, published hashes of the private product ADRs, and signed commits. The rulesets on main and tags, and the ADR check in CI, are already done (ADR-0103).
blockedBy: Owner decision (mirror step; signed commits decided there)
unlocks: Make `verify` a required check on main
items.landNowWhy: The owner decides the mirror and signed commits at the mirror step. Making it public also fires the trigger of the required-check row.

items.title: Funding, patents and legal entity
items.summary: Decide and disclose who pays for Study 1 and their role, and whether any patent is filed. Any filing goes in before Stage 1 and must never delay publication. Same as D9.
items.landNowWhy: The owner's decision.

items.title: Ratify the 15 by-continuation ADRs and settle the Proposed records
items.summary: One pass that ratifies the 15 records, accepts ADR-0034 to 0038 as amended, adopts SM-1 to SM-6, the port-rule wording and the CR11 interpretation (the Monitor co-signs), accepts or rejects ADR-0039 and ADR-0040, settles the ADR-0006, 0019 and 0020 follow-ups, and confirms ADR-0041's rules.
items.landNowWhy: This is the owner's review. Part of it needs the Monitor's co-signature. The index still lists 15 by-continuation records and 7 Proposed.

items.title: Confirm the baseline set
items.summary: Duplicate of D1: the default is B-Skill, B-Outside and B-BoN, gated behind H1a.
items.landNowWhy: The owner's decision.

items.title: Fill in the product-consequences table ('Worse' rows)
items.summary: CR10 requires the table in the Stage 1 report. Same as D24.
items.landNowWhy: Due before Stage 1, after D1.

items.title: Clear licences (frontend-design SKILL.md; provider output terms)
items.summary: Clear the licence of the SKILL.md that B-Skill uses, and the providers' output terms, before generated pages are released under CR13.
items.landNowWhy: Not due until Stage 0. The legal reviewer is not yet found.

items.title: Rename the local ActAI folder or retire it
items.summary: C:\Users\arvik\OneDrive\Documents\ActAI still exists. Rename or retire it in favour of the byway checkout, and carry the Claude project memory across.
items.landNowWhy: Nothing blocks it, but it is the owner's folder outside the repository, it still holds the protocol originals, and the ADR index advises doing it at the end of a session. Low value.

items.title: Review the 38 Delegated records
items.summary: The owner reviews the ADRs Claude decided under delegated authority, starting with ADR-0071, 0072, 0074, 0076, 0077 and 0078. Any change is recorded in a new ADR. The index still counts 38.

items.landNowWhy: Nothing blocks it, and the playbook says any time. Only the owner can review. The product records that govern live use (ADR-0074 security model, ADR-0095 spend book) make a natural first batch before real money flows.

items.title: Protect the product's provider keys before the first live run
items.summary: Set a spending limit, or the smallest prepaid balance, in each provider's console (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, fal) for the keys in .env.agents. Rotate any real key the dev server had in its environment on 2026-10-07.

unlocks: First live run with real keys and real money
items.landNowWhy: Nothing blocks it, and it gates owner goal 1. Only the owner can do it, because the keys and consoles are the owner's. No reply to the 2026-10-08 rotation request is recorded.

items.title: Complete protocol v1.1's verification log (B.3) and open checks (B.2)
items.summary: A human checks each of B.3's 29 claims against its primary source; none is verified yet. The B.2 checks include retirement dates, frame terms, power_sim3 certification, the Stage 0 names and hashes, Judge hosting, the Monitor key backup, the HEDS and CONSORT templates, spike tests, the throughput plan and the CR10 tables.

items.landNowWhy: The B.3 checks need a human. Several B.2 items wait on the Monitor, the transcription, the cost probe or the harness. Claude-only parts such as the templates are research-track work not yet resumed.

items.landNowWhy: At risk: the target month is now, and the questions are not recorded as sent.

items.summary: File the Stage 0 registration. It needs every blocking decision closed and its marker removed, the prompts transcribed, and the B.3 log completed.
blockedBy: "Product data never feeds a study" against ADR-0041 rule 3
items.landNowWhy: Most of its prerequisites are owner or outside actions, and none of them has started.

items.summary: The all-arm pilot; only the Monitor sees its results. Under ADR-0047 its results are unblinded only after Stage 0.
items.landNowWhy: It needs the harness's P0 tier (the protocol assumes 2 full-time engineers), which is parked until the owner resumes the research track.

items.landNowWhy: Downstream of the pilot.

graph.summary: Edge convention: from -> to. 'blocks' means from must happen before to; 'unlocks' means finishing from makes to possible; 'triggers' means from (an event, or landing an item) fires to's stated trigger; 'feeds' means from gives evidence or a partial input, not a hard prerequisite. There are 232 items (backlog and playbook), 9 milestones and 25 external blockers (ext-*), with 333 edges, all checked against the backlog text and acyclic. GOAL 1 critical path: Claude re-checks the model ids and price rows (no keys, no paid calls; the readings are dated 2026-10-07). The owner sets spending limits at the five providers and rotates the 2026-10-07 keys. The owner then runs one Balanced run under $1 and compares byway's records with each provider's dashboard. Nothing in the code blocks it. The run then brings back about ten rows: served-model labels, planning numbers, the Gemini and billing checks, C3 trims, the Custom-profile revisit, the runbooks. Further real use needs two owner choices: the C2 mood-boards decision before C2 runs on Best or OpenAI, and one paid fal link before C5 runs. LAND NOW, no owner decision, in 5 batches: B1 is the money path before the live run (8 rows, M); B2 rescues the decision record from %TEMP% and pins C1-H (4 rows, L); B3 stops paid images being lost and fixes their notes (4 rows, M, one Delegated ADR); B4 adds renderer observability and tests (4 rows); B5 is optional polish. A coupling the owner should see: P2 (activity inputs by reference) is itself a workflow-bundle change. Landing it is the 'next deliberate bundle change' that four chores and the VOICE-RETRY choice wait for, and it also fires the content-layer row's trigger, whose first step is a paid pilot (~$6-30). It is cheapest before live runs exist (ADR-0078 ends waiting runs), so scheduling it is an owner call, not land-now. Corrections to the classified input: fal's host set is not blocked by the first live run, which leaves C5 out; it needs the owner's paid fal link with fal's spending limit set. estimate-voice-free can land before voice.apply is retired, so the edge runs the other way. v12-bbon-n -> B-BoN price was removed because it made a false cycle (the ceiling uses the planning figure). The renderer environment allowlist and macOS depended on each other; that is now modelled as macOS feeding the allowlist. Duplicate decisions point into one canonical node: D1/act-confirm-baseline-set, D9/act-funding-patents-entity, D13/price-set-spending-ceiling, D24/act-product-consequences-table, D10/act-ratify-adrs. RESEARCH: Stage 0 (~2027-02-01) is at risk. The venue questions are due this month and not recorded as sent; the Monitor is due ~mid-November; the transcription is due 2026-11-30 and needs a second transcriber; the harness (XL) gates the pilot. The decision queue is sorted by reach through hard edges. By the owner's goal order, the keys step (#7) and the first live run (#12) come first. The venue questions (#3) are the most time-sensitive, due this month. Read-only checks for the owner's other questions: no ADR cites a path inside a git worktree. The one remaining worktree, .claude/worktrees/admiring-agnesi-9896e0 on branch fix/flaky-ledger-tamper-mtime at 3822920, is clean and merged into main. The evidence at risk is in %TEMP%, not in the worktrees (B2). The ADR index's open-decisions table still names no outcome ADRs (r3-outcome-pointers, in B2). Scratch files: C:\Users\arvik\AppData\Local\Temp\byway-fixes\scratch\backlog-map\map-builder\ (build.py, final.py, final.json).

gaps.what: The owner's standing rules for checking code and for fix rounds exist only in Claude's auto-memory on this machine. No repo record has them. The rules: every code change gets an independent adversarial check before it is pushed, in bigger blocks; no further fix round starts, and none is ruled out, without the owner. git grep of docs/, README.md and the playbook at 8401820 finds neither rule. ADR-0103 has only the pnpm verify merge gate and the 'risky change runs CI on its branch first' step. ADR-0081 has only the one-off bounded round 14. ADR-0104 and ADR-0103 mention single checks as history, not as a rule. ADR-0062 (code first, also taken from a memory rule) is the precedent for a Process ADR. Correction to the draft: 'docs-only commits ride with the next checked batch', 'hand fixes go into the next check' and what a checker does are Claude's practice (adversarial-check-before-push.md, 'How to apply'), not the owner's words. Under the quote-verbatim lesson they belong in the delegated part. gaps.row: | Engine-thread stalls on slow machines (the Windows CI write-up's option 6) | The investigation behind ADR-0106 measured pauses of byway's own process of 2.5 to 4.1 s on the owner's machine pinned to 2 CPUs under load, and up to 9.5 s at start-up under bursts of starvation. During a pause, timers fire late: a close is judged late (since ADR-0106 that costs one relaunch; row "What the late-close fix left", item 1), and fixed waits run out. On CI's Windows machine, Temporal's own SQLite store timed out ("context deadline exceeded"), and its calls took up to 12 s (run 39152075629; row "Known Windows timing flake"). Likely sources: the spend book's money transactions commit with synchronous=FULL on the engine's thread (packages/store/src/spend-book.ts). node:sqlite's DatabaseSync holds the thread while it waits out its 10 s busy timeout on the file the web app also writes (db.ts). On CI, the e2e data folder sits under the system temp folder on the runner's throttled C: disk (scripts/e2e.ts). And plain CPU starvation. A person's slow machine (on battery, under antivirus, a slow disk, a VM) can see the same. The write-up (2026-10-18) said to keep this because it is the one option that also helps slow user machines. Moving the synchronous commits off the engine's thread is product work with its own design and checks (the spend book's durability is ADR-0095's); moving CI's data folder off C: is a workflow change. Pick up when a live run or a kept server log shows stalls, or if Windows CI still goes red on timing once the tests' time limits are gone | store (spend-book.ts, db.ts), runner (worker), scripts/e2e.ts, .github/workflows/verify.yml |

findings.title: F01 — Make executable semantics authoritative (byway-review.md lines 124, 145-157; docs-advisor-review.md A1 and A3; engine-protocol-review.md E6)
findings.severity: P1 (review P1); the prompt binding part P2; the operator and gate-feed mismatches P3
findings.rootCause: Admission and execution use two definitions of what a recipe does. Admission reads self-declared annotations (writes, the 'voice' port, block labels) and structural approximations ('always runs' = not in an optional or route; a flow walk that runs every loop body to its end). It ignores variant, containers, gate feeds, loop exit points and the operators that put another version in place of the work. Execution derives all of these from actor, role, produces artifact, medium, variant and the enclosing operator, and nothing requires a declaration to agree with execution (verification lines 112-129, 170-176).
findings.how: The P1 root cause is removed and guarded. @byway/recipe/semantics.ts defines the executed semantics once: the effects table, personWrite/voiceWrite/authorWrite, voiceScope, BLOCK_OF_ROLE, exitPoints/runsEveryTime, gateFeed and FIELD_ROLES. The validator (ST12 writer-undeclared/voice-*/block-role/set-aside/pick-*, PR6 on executed voice, ST9/ST10 human-write, scope set-aside), the composed profile (COMP-1 over runsEveryTime, a writer allowance per VOICE, COMPOSED-PROMPT by output contract plus a dry render with slotsForStep, and from ADR-0097 promptShows) and web start (Advisor.admit re-admits the stored recipe: 400 or 409) read it. The interpreter imports machineWrites, voiceWrite and feedsGate. A run-time PR6 guard (interpreter.ts:291) stops any machine write after the person's words that lacks keepsVoice, keepsVoice checks every held VOICE (ports.held), and a C pick whose judge names no draft fails instead of taking A. Agreement tests hold the module to the runner (parserFor, human writes, loop exits), and corpus tests (declaration monotonicity 3,952 changes, placement soundness 3,453 moves) guard regressions. All of the review's probes, re-run on main in my clone, are refused (the C4 hidden writer gives PR6, ST12 writer-undeclared and COMPOSED-VOICE; both prompt swaps give COMPOSED-PROMPT). What is only partly done: (1) the operator port disagreements (audit, one-shot gate, each) were settled by aligning validator/src/scope.ts (AUDIT_OUT, its gate case) to the interpreter. These semantics still live in two places, not in the shared module. No executed test compares the interpreter's audit, gate and each outputs with scope typing, which is the review's explicit acceptance item. A mutation in my clone that dropped the critique from the interpreter's audit and gate outputs failed only the bundle-hash pin in build.test.ts across 1,272 unit tests (e2e not run). (2) Set-aside (a pick, keep-or-revert or scored loop after the person's words) is enforced only at admission. Runner.start and the workflow run no product policy and no run-time set-aside, by a deliberate, delegated choice in ADR-0092, so a direct Runner.start of an unadmitted recipe is protected only by the PR6 guard and the held voice.

findings.title: F02 — Bound total work before constructing it (byway-review.md lines 125, 159-167; docs-advisor-review.md A2)
findings.rootCause: Nothing at any admission layer bounds the counts that shape work (replicate n, loop max, relay maxLinks, lens count, nesting depth and size), and nothing says where a gate's retry may sit. The schema accepts any int, the validator sets only lower bounds, the profile checks only knobs, Runner.start only parses, and the interpreter expands eagerly. Batch bytes are width x per-activity input, and every activity input carries run-level and path-level data by value: seeds and option lists grow quadratically with the counts, and run inputs are set by the person. The count-determined part belongs in the engine's bound; the root fix for both parts is carrying that data by reference, a separate item (lines 195-197).
findings.how: The count-determined root cause is removed at every entry. parseRecipe checks a shape bound iteratively before any recursive walk (64 levels of JSON, 10,000 op nodes, 1 MiB) and reports it as a ZodError, and checkAnswer turns any other throw into COMPOSED-INTERNAL. ENGINE_LIMITS (peak 500, 2,000 step runs, 3 gate retries, 2 MiB batch bytes counting every seed the run can hand out plus option ids and views) and workBound are enforced as ST3 'limit' at compose, by engineProblems at Runner.start (RecipeRefused before createRun) and inside run.ts at workflow start. ST10 'retry-scope' keeps a retrying gate out of fan-outs (G1). COMPOSED_LIMITS (n 16, loop 12, relay 8, lenses 4, peak 32, 400 runs, depth 12, 100 nodes, 32 KiB) cover model-authored recipes. The review's 1e9 probe, re-run on main, gives ST3:limit and COMPOSED-LIMIT, and n=17 gives COMPOSED-LIMIT. Not done: the byte half of the root cause the verification itself named. Run inputs (the brief with up to 5 x 200,000-character attachments, the fixed voice deck, ports.held and ports.voice) are still carried by value in every activity input, so canonical C1/C2 can still wedge in 'running' with very large attachments, the F02 failure mode. That item is in the backlog with no trigger. A runtime concurrency limiter was deliberately not built, replaced by the static peak bound at every entry. Prompt cancellation of a large valid plan is not separately tested.

findings.title: Give each paid operation a durable identity and accounting lifecycle (byway-review.md:169-187; sources gateway-store-review.md GS-01, GS-03, GS-04 and engine-protocol-review.md E1)
findings.severity: P2 (review P1). Every leak is bounded or needs an unusual trigger: the cross-process overrun is limited to the workspace cap and one advisor estimate; the memo overlap needs a Temporal timeout or a dead worker; a torn ledger needs an OS crash, power loss or a full disk; a fal re-buy costs $0.35-1.70 per clip (lines 639-644)
findings.verdict: ACCEPT_PARTLY (verification §1 line 30; cluster B section line 602)
findings.rootCause: Between admission and settlement the gateway kept no durable, shared record of a paid call. Exposure existed only as one process's in-memory reservation (gateway.ts:130) or as a settled JSONL line read leniently (ledger.ts:242). fal acceptance lived on the stack (fal.ts:127-129). The memo recorded results only after the effect (memo.ts:85-103). Nothing decided whether a failed attempt might have been billed: retries were blind, split between the SDK's hidden policy and a classifier that misread wrapped errors (lines 646-652). A separate, minor root cause at the UI edge: the GET render creates the recommendation as a side effect, and a run start carries no identity from the caller (line 654)
findings.how: The main root cause is gone on main. The spend book in byway.sqlite (contracts SpendBook, store migrations 6 and 7) is now the cap authority, shared by the web process and the worker. Each method is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, and the money transactions commit at synchronous=FULL. A call is admitted as open at its estimate, marked sent just before its first request, recorded as accepted with fal's request ids before polling, then settled at its true cost (idempotent), released (never billed) or abandoned as uncertain. A sent call that loses its lease becomes uncertain and counts against the workspace cap until the person clears it, so an expired lease never erases liability. GatewayOptions.spendBook is required, so no root can go back to per-process reservations (ADR-0095). One billingOf() classification, which walks err.cause, decides every retry. fal jobs are submitted once by REST POST with redirect:'error', and a 'maybe' submit is never re-sent (ADR-0091). Each step's paid call carries an operation key (run + memo key) held while its invocation lives. An overlapping attempt is refused in-flight and waits for the memo. A settled call answers settledEarlier, so the waiter looks for the kept result before it buys again. An accepted fal job whose holder is gone is resumed from its stored ids (ADR-0099). Ledger lines are absorbed idempotently into the book. A complete line that cannot be recorded becomes a fault that refuses paid admission until acknowledged. A torn tail is copied to ledger.jsonl.damaged-<stamp>-<pid> and the chain continues. Only the outbox drain appends, so a busy or failed ledger delays the entry, never the call or the caps. Run starts accept a validated client UUID, return the same run for the same inputs and give 409 otherwise (ADR-0099 decision 7). One exception: the minor UI sub-cause (paid work inside the Recommendation page's GET render) is fixed only at the symptom. Concurrent first loads share one advisor call per process (ADR-0091 decision 6), and the render can still call the model (page.tsx:47 -> recommendationOrProblem -> firstRecommendation). This follows the verification's own deliberate choice (line 1145), and it is filed without a trigger.

findings.title: Separate cost estimates from enforceable caps (byway-review.md:189-197; source gateway-store-review.md GS-02)
findings.severity: P2 (review P1). The overshoot is limited to one extra attempt for each refused or sticky-routed call already in flight. It needs a classifier refusal, which is uncommon here, plus admission just below the cap. Later spend is refused because settlement is correct. Demo mode is unaffected (lines 690-696)
findings.verdict: ACCEPT_PARTLY (verification §1 line 31; cluster B section line 659)
findings.rootCause: Two wrong assumptions (lines 698-702). (1) Admission assumed one billing plan, one attempt on the requested model. But the Anthropic adapter opted every request into a server-side refusal fallback, which can bill a second attempt, or a sticky-routed first attempt, on another model Anthropic picks. Settlement also silently substituted the requested rate for any served model with no price row. (2) The code and UI treated heuristic token estimates as guaranteed upper bounds ('estimates err high'), and an image of unknown size defaulted to 5000 tokens, below the code's own 6400 cap.
findings.how: Root cause (1) is removed. ADR-0102 (owner D1 = 2b) removes every way to ask for a fallback. AnthropicAdapterOptions is { client } only. anthropicParams sends no beta header and no fallbacks field (anthropic.ts:40-72). GatewayOptions.anthropicRefusalFallback and REFUSAL_FALLBACK_BETA are gone. OpenRouter stays pinned with allow_fallbacks:false. A source guard over packages/*/src, apps/web/src, apps/web/app and scripts fails on any fallback request. So every dispatch bills the model it was admitted for, and sticky routing cannot happen. A decline gets one retry on the same model (askOnceMore in gateway.ts). The retry is a paid call of its own, admitted in the spend book against both caps, with its own operation key, and settled and ledgered with retryOf. Settlement prices each billed attempt at its own row. A served model with no row is priced at the requested row and flagged priceBasis 'assumed', which is recorded in the hash chain and shown in Settings (ADR-0091 decision 3). Root cause (2) is removed by contract (ADR-0091 decision 4; ADR-0102 decision 6). estimate.ts, spec §3.4, the README and the screens say planning estimates, not bounds. Non-ASCII text counts at its UTF-8 bytes. An unreadable image counts at 6400, and WebP sizes are now read (e3c4e6b). The UI says 'Estimated cost' and 'Estimates can be low ...'. A guard test keeps bound claims and fallback-overrun wording out. What remains is the estimate's own error: a call can settle above its reservation, the true cost is recorded, and later admission refuses against it. That is stated, not bounded.

findings.title: F05: Enforce script consent on full-size views (Full-size HTML serves a more permissive execution policy than its preview)
findings.severity: P2 (review P1), first in the P2 order. Exploiting it needs hostile page content and a click, and only that one document's text (plus IP and timing) can leave
findings.verdict: ACCEPT: every claim holds at b33f1285; both verifiers reproduced the leak on a production build
findings.rootCause: One URL (/artifacts/<id>) serves one response policy to two viewing contexts. CSP sandbox flags intersect with the iframe's sandbox attribute, so for the per-page switch to work the route always granted 'sandbox allow-scripts', and consent lived only in the embedding iframe, never in the response. Any top-level navigation (Open links, fallbacks, Markdown links, typed URLs, history) got the scriptable policy, and the one-year immutable cache kept those responses alive. A second gap: the app CSP had no frame-src, so a framed page could be navigated off-site.
findings.how: Consent now lives in the response, not only in the frame. pageCsp(origin, scripts) in apps/web/src/server/artifacts.ts ends in a bare 'sandbox' unless pageScriptsGranted(url, headers) holds: ?scripts=1, no download, sec-fetch-dest iframe, sec-fetch-site same-origin. Any ask for scripts is answered Cache-Control no-store. artifactResponse (api.ts:427-455) takes request.headers from the route, and the media route never grants. The inert default never depends on the request, so every top-level path (links, typed URLs, history, future links) gets an inert page served after the fix. ScaledPage and PageResult take an id and derive src and sandbox from one boolean. Every in-app Open uses openHref → /view/<id> (app/view/[id]/page.tsx), which shows a page in PageResult with the per-visit switch. A grep of src and app found exactly one place that builds the /artifacts/ path (api.ts:79). The app CSP in next.config.ts:62 has frame-src 'self'. Mutation checks in my clone confirm tests catch the cause returning. With the CSP set back to always 'sandbox allow-scripts', 4 of the 7 consent-boundary.spec cases fail (control passes; the frame-src cases need the second mutation) and 4 server/api unit tests fail. With frame-src 'self' removed, the 2 frame-navigation cases fail. Together that is 6 of 7, matching ADR-0085's claim. A later gap is closed: Markdown own-artifact links with ?query/#fragment opened the raw (inert) address until 730ebc7 (ADR-0100 item 7).

findings.title: F06 — Preserve unsent human work across inspection
findings.severity: P1 (review P1); at the P1/P2 boundary, kept P1 because the reset text can be sent at once as 'Your words' (verification:1740)
findings.rootCause: Person-authored input has no owner that outlives the component that shows it. Each panel keeps its draft in its own useState, seeded from the checkpoint, so the draft lives exactly as long as the YourTurn mount. Inspection, run end, a stale poll that drops the active checkpoint and a reload all unmount the panel, and the next mount re-seeds from cp.initialText. There is no checkpoint-keyed store above that boundary, no session persistence, and no rule that only server state settles a draft. The same assumption ties Start attachments and Recommendation examples to their mount (verification:1742, cluster root 1731).
findings.how: The draft's owner moved from the panel to the Run screen. RunScreen.tsx:106-123 creates one createDraftStore(runId) per mount (the page keys RunScreen by run id, app/runs/[id]/page.tsx:24), above the work area's conditional render. A draft is keyed by checkpoint id. The kinds write, react, directive, pick and select go to sessionStorage through sessionSlot.ts (versioned envelope, every access guarded). The store is settled only by snapshots the refresher applied (the `served` flag, RunScreen.tsx:117-122), never by `initial` or by an unmount. All eight answering panels seed once from `draft` and write through `onDraft` (panels/*.tsx). A successful POST marks the answer sent, for every kind, which locks it read-only (draftStore.markSent; TurnFooter shows 'Sent'). Text left on a closed question is shown as UnsentWords, read-only with Copy and Discard and no send. YourTurn renders only once the drafts have loaded, so it never flashes initialText. The same helper keeps Start attachments (startDraft.ts) and Recommendation examples (examplesDraft.ts). The pre-merge re-check (22b0400) fixed two more defects test-first. Back without a reload had deleted the draft (settle now keeps a draft whose question is unlisted while the run goes on). The Sent lock had been editable (put now ignores changes to a sent draft).

findings.verdict: ACCEPT. Every technical claim reproduces at b33f1285 (verification line 34, 2068-2076).
findings.rootCause: Verification lines 2038-2047 and 2110-2119. The person's copy could be written or rewritten by something other than an exact, total application of their edit (a model, a lossy fallback, a reader that skips or misreads, a tokenizer that is not the browser's, a later machine writer whose lock scope is guessed or fails open), as long as the result passed a check weaker than the edit. findings.title: F08 — Explain actual composition changes (byway-review.md lines 131, 231-239; docs-advisor-review.md A4)
findings.rootCause: diffFromNearest is a hand-written comparer over a hand-picked subset of fields and node types, and its default is unsafe: 'same' means 'none of the compared fields differ', not 'semantically equal'. No shared definition says which fields, node types and placements affect execution, and the explainers read declared flags and a coarse pick mapping instead of executed semantics (line 214).
findings.how: The unsafe default is gone. sameRun compares semantic projections built from FIELD_ROLES, a mapped type over every schema object (an unclassified field fails typecheck, and a test holds it to the zod schema object by object). Names are dropped, sets sorted, and seq nesting and consumes/reads order kept. Every node type is paired. Picks ('chosen at random, no one compares them'), the gate bar ('stops at a lower quality bar', never quoted), early stops, VOICE scope, optional/route questions, reads, retries and moves across containers, exit points or past your words get specific lines, and any other projection difference reads 'Other technical changes that affect how it runs'. present.ts reads the effects table, voiceScope and appliesCritique (later promptShows) instead of declared writes. Web start re-admits and returns 409 if the stored explanation changed. Both review probes, re-run on main, now read 'Changed: Pick one (Refine): chosen at random, no one compares them, where you chose before' and 'Changed: Outside critique repeats: stops at a lower quality bar'. A single-field mutation test over every semantic field of C1-C7 guards its return. One recorded departure: a consumes reorder reads 'Other technical changes', because image order changes what the model sees (ADR-0098 decision 5).

findings.title: C5's shot critic observes the storyboard/still instead of the actual clip (byway-review.md:133, 251-259; sub-review engine-protocol-review.md E4, lines 61-69; probe engine-probes.json c5VideoReview)
findings.rootCause: Render is never told which relay link it renders, and the clip's own frames are never bound to its shot: the media view was defined once as 'whole storyboard text plus each shot's pre-chain ASSET still'; relayLink recorded clipArtifactId but not the last frame the gateway already returned; the interpreter knew ports.shot and linkStart but did not pass them to render. The check-clean loop also had no 'could not observe' outcome, so missing evidence became 'No defects.' or futile repairs (lines 2867-2877). The verification withdrew 'the gateway contract carries images only' as a cause (line 2875, 3391).
findings.how: The verification's root cause is removed on main. relayLink writes clipArtifactId and lastFrameArtifactId together (runner/src/activities/relay.ts:100); the interpreter passes link {shot, startFrame} to render only while a link runs (interpreter.ts:312), and relay() clears shot/linkStart on exit (interpreter.ts:782). render.ts linkView (lines 93-106) shows only that shot's line plus 'The frame this clip starts from:' and 'The last frame of the generated clip:', or returns `unobservable` with noClipNote when the clip or last frame is missing. unobservable() (interpreter.ts:794-799) skips a model check or critic only inside a link whose view has nothing to judge, and the loop exits 'unchecked' (interpreter.ts:301, 573). product.c5.shot-check v2 says it sees the line, the start frame and the last frame, reports only defects the clip introduced, and says motion cannot be seen; the Motion explainer says the same. The review's 'observe motion' option is not built; it took the 'explicitly limit' branch: the check's wording is limited (not renamed), and middle-frame sampling is in the backlog. Tests passed in the clone. Mutations were caught: render ignoring link fails three link-view tests (M3); a judge asked with nothing to see fails the C5 no-video e2e (M8). The final-check residual about the rule being 'worded backwards' (line 3411) did not reach code: the guard returns undefined when ports.shot is undefined, and the no-video e2e shows the launch-gate critic after the chain still called twice.

findings.title: C3 prompt allows no illustration while runtime requires one (byway-review.md:134, 261-269; sub-review engine-protocol-review.md E5, lines 71-79; probe engine-extra-probes.json noImages)
findings.severity: P3 (review P2); borderline P2 only on the worst case
findings.rootCause: Two wrong assumptions (lines 2908-2914): (1) the runtime decided image cardinality by medium (checkBriefs: at least one, at most the slots knob, via Math.max(1, cap)) while each prompt states its own count, so there were two definitions that disagreed; (2) a well-formed short answer had no honest degraded outcome: askModel's single repair retry turned a second short answer into a fatal ContractMissed, though assetStep already had a pass-through convention (asset.ts:97-99). Separately, C3's prompt gave the model a veto over the person's opt-in at the optional gate.
findings.how: The two causes were fixed in ADR-0090 without waiting for D3, and D3 is now decided and built. (1) The count belongs to the prompt: every image-briefs template declares `images:` (template.ts requires it there and refuses it elsewhere); the renderer returns RenderedPrompt.images, and assetStep builds the free plan from it inside the parse callback (asset.ts:122-123, slot-plan.ts freePlan). That also settles the final-check ordering residual (line 3412). Declarations on main: article.ASSET 1-3, helper@web-page 1-3, helper@prose 0-3, product.c3.asset 1-1 (v3), each on media and options. A min-0 prompt answering zero finishes not skipped with NO_IMAGE_CHOSEN_NOTE; zero usable briefs finish skipped with NO_BRIEF_NOTE, so a deliberate no-image is told apart from a failed provider. findings.title: F13: Make evidence completeness explicit (Human and model review views silently omit artifact content)
findings.severity: P2 (review P2). No stored data is lost, but decisions (TELLS compare, C7 step rows, GREAT ranks that gate loops) can be made on partial evidence without notice
findings.verdict: ACCEPT: both halves hold. Minor overstatements (JSON over 16 KB is uncommon, U+FFFD is cosmetic, the write editor holds the full initialText) do not change the verdict
findings.rootCause: A representation built for a lighter context is reused in a decision context and cannot say it is partial. (a) ArtifactInfo had one overloaded 'text' field: a byte prefix built for step rows and contact sheets, with nothing marking it as a prefix, so decision views rendered it as the artifact and row summaries counted from it. (b) BLIND-1 cards assumed an item's words fit one 2,576 px tile: fit was estimated, not measured; overflow was clipped silently by CSS; and in cards form the card was the only carrier of the words, because the text slot held CARD_NOTE.
findings.how: (a) ArtifactInfo (apps/web/src/view/rundata.ts:13-29) is now {mediaType, excerpt?, complete?, bytes?, diffstat?, titles?}. artifactInfo (apps/web/src/server/run-data.ts) streaming-decodes the first 16,000 bytes, so it never ends in half a character, and computes diffstat and option titles from the whole bytes. The rename forced every consumer to choose a snippet, the whole text or a server fact, and a guard scan in evidence.test.ts limits who reads or sets .excerpt (3584a41 extends it to destructuring and element access). Large previews (ArtifactPreview size='large', used by Compare, References, StepDetail and RunStatusPanel) call useWholeText → loadWholeText, which keeps one promise per content-addressed id and evicts failures. Until the text arrives they show PartialNotice with sizes that always differ and an openHref link. TextPreview parses JSON only from whole text, StepThumbs reads diffstat and titles, PickPanel and ComparePanel give every option an Open. (b) cardHtml has no max-height or overflow:hidden. fitCard measures every render and fails closed ('too-tall'/'empty' → StepError naming the item, never tiles[0]). Text critics' cards carry a fixed line and the full words go in the view under each label (critic.ts buildLineup), rendered once with cut:false. Image-only critics get a measured cut with a visible '[… N more words not shown]' line, a card2/ JSON memo with the cut, Lineup.cut by item, and a cutNote appended to the step note (e934f6b; ADR-0090). 88f0a77 makes the fit search converge. Mutations in my clone confirm the tests catch the causes returning. The old byte-prefix decode with diffstat/titles from the prefix fails 3 evidence.test cases. Keeping the first tile plus a CARD_NOTE-only text view fails 6 cards/critic tests. Removing the note push fails the step-note test. One limit stays by design: for image-only critics (C5 gate, web-page) words beyond one tile at 12 px still do not reach the critic. That cut is measured, visible and disclosed, not silent, and the verification rated this branch 'partly'.

findings.title: F14 — Recover the recommendation state after a successful retry
findings.severity: P2 (review P2), low-end: the in-app Settings path remounts and works (verification:1751)
findings.rootCause: The screen has no rule for which server state it owns and how that state changes. The recommendation, and a selection derived from it with an invented 'c4' fallback, are copied into useState once at mount, while the screen-mode gate and remainingUsd read live props. The only re-read path, router.refresh(), re-runs a server render that is not a pure read: it makes the first recommendation (F03). So a 'refresh the live props' step can both put owned state out of step with the props and trigger a model call nobody asked for. Recovery is a props refresh, not a state transition, so the gate and the body disagree and a client-made default is shown as the person's choice (verification:1753).
findings.how: RecommendationView now owns one RecState, seeded once by initialRecState (selection = chosenRecipeId ?? rec?.recipeId ?? null, so no 'c4') and never re-seeded from props. Try again POSTs {ensure:true}, and recommendCommand calls currentRecommendation, which returns the stored recommendation or makes and stores one. flip and compose are commands too. Each returns {recommendation|composed, remainingUsd}, with the remaining amount read after the command (api.ts:203-216), and is applied by recovered, rerouted or composedReady in one setState. RecommendationView no longer calls router.refresh(): grep finds it only in SettingsView and SpendingRecords, whose renders are pure reads. screen() shows the failure panel only when nothing else can be shown. 'Your choice' appears only for an alternative the person picked. page.tsx:57-58 keys the view by `${intakeId}:${chosenRecipeId}`. The impure first-recommendation GET render itself remains (F03): concurrent first loads are deduped by ADR-0091 and ADR-0099, and moving it off the render is filed in the backlog.

findings.title: F15 — Do not regress run state when polls arrive out of order
findings.severity: P3 (review P2): the display regression heals within one poll interval, nothing wrong can be persisted, and the meter is already monotone; the lasting harms are a sticky false-offline banner on ended runs and, through F06, a lost draft (verification:1762)
findings.rootCause: Server snapshots reach the client (RunScreen, and Nav's waiting count in the same way) through several overlapping, uncancellable requests with no single owner of the request sequence. Each response is applied, and sets the connection state, in arrival order. mergeRunData is right to treat a snapshot as authoritative; what is missing is control over which snapshot reaches it (verification:1764).
findings.how: Each screen now has one owner of its request sequence. createRefresher (view/refresh.ts) bumps a generation and aborts the previous request on now(); poll() joins the in-flight request. Only a request that is still the latest, not disposed and not aborted may apply data or set the connection state. A request this instance aborted never sets 'lost'. A request unanswered after 30 s (body included) counts as lost and applies nothing. useRefresher creates and disposes one instance per key (runId for RunScreen, pathname for Nav) and re-reads the server-rendered snapshot through the same path. usePolling re-arms only after a poll settles and skips hidden tabs. RunScreen polls at LOST_RETRY_MS while the connection is lost, whatever the status, so the banner clears on ended runs. mergeRunData is unchanged: with ordered apply, 'latest snapshot wins' holds, because each applied snapshot was read after the previous applied one arrived. R3 (answerable = open AND not ended) guards the one tear that can stick. get(), post() and patch() treat a successful status with an unreadable body as a failure. The review's server snapshot revision and consistent view() reads were deliberately not built (ADR-0082) and are filed with triggers.

findings.title: F16: Sanitize successful gateway results before persistence (summary table: 'Secret sanitation protects evidence copies but not outgoing results'; sub-review gateway-store-review.md GS-05)
findings.rootCause: Nothing enforces the key promise where a key can cross a boundary. The only secret mechanism, makeRedactor, ran only on the gateway's own diagnostic copies (wire bodies, error strings). Four crossings were unchecked: outbound request text before dispatch; inbound completion text before it reaches runner, advisor and memos; inbound provider metadata (servedModel, upstreamProvider) before ledger and results; user material at the browser-to-server boundary before it is stored and shown. redact.ts:22-23, ADR-0074 and spec §2 claimed more than the code did (verification lines 3452-3457, cluster statement 3419-3430).
findings.how: All four unchecked crossings named in the verification's root cause are now checked by one exact rule, and each check has a test that fails when it is removed (mutation runs in a scratch clone). (1) Browser to server: parseBody(request, schema, heldKeyIn) runs findHeldKey over every string of the parsed body, property names included (strings-in.ts). It returns a 400 naming the variable before anything is stored (http.ts:41-62). Every route that reads a JSON body passes deps.heldKeyIn: intakes, intakes/[id]/recommend, refs, runs, runs/[id]/control, checkpoints, spend, settings PATCH and renderer PATCH. (2) Gateway out: refuseHeldKeys runs after validation and before profile resolution, reservation, exposure or dispatch, in complete() (system and every text part, gateway.ts:221, requestTexts l.1052), image() (l.331) and video() (l.513). (3) Gateway in: after record() has ledgered the call with redacted evidence, findHeldKey runs on out.text (gateway.ts:304-309). A hit throws a non-retryable provider-error with the heldKey marker, billed and settled, so the text never reaches CompletionResult, memos or artifacts. It also runs on the after-decline retry, since that reuses completeOnce. (4) Metadata: record() normalises labels (providerLabel, F19) and then scrubs them (scrubLabels, gateway.ts:903-910, 1047), and the results return the ledger's scrubbed value. Error paths stay redacted. makeRedactor's comment was corrected, and it now also scrubs each held-key ':'-part (redact.ts:33), which closes the final-check residual. asset.ts:247 rethrows isHeldKeyError, and modelProblem maps held-key errors to 400 and 502. ADR-0088 amends ADR-0074's Keys bullet without editing it; spec §2 Keys (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-product-v1-design.md:42) now says what is enforced and what is not. Follow-ups stop the browser tab keeping a refused paste on Start, examples and run answers (ADR-0100 item 10).

findings.title: F17: Restrict media retrieval and enforce limits while streaming (summary table: 'Provider media fetch trusts destinations and buffers before checking size'; sub-review gateway-store-review.md GS-06)
findings.rootCause: download() in fal.ts:87-98 trusts any URL fal names once its scheme is https, and leaves the rest to fetch's defaults and provider-API conventions: no host, port or userinfo policy, and redirects followed to any host, http downgrade included; a size ceiling only through the optional, encoded-length Content-Length and a check after full buffering; the clip typed from headers; CDN statuses classified as provider-API statuses (401 read as a missing key). The intent in the comments was never implemented, and no ADR recorded how far provider media is trusted (l.3480-3485).
findings.how: download() in packages/gateway/src/providers/fal.ts (l.208-251) no longer leaves destination, size, type or status to defaults. admitMediaUrl (l.161-163: https:, empty username and password, port '', hostname matching /^(?:[a-z0-9-]+[.])*fal[.]media$/) runs before the first fetch (l.215) and on every resolved Location (l.231). fetch is called with redirect:'manual' and one AbortSignal.timeout covering every hop (l.216-220). A 3xx without a Location is refused, and more than MAX_REDIRECTS=3 hops are refused. A non-ok media status throws mediaError('provider-error'), retryable only for 408, 429 and 5xx (l.236-239), so a CDN 401 can no longer become no-credentials (relay.ts:90 skips only on no-credentials). A declared length over the cap is refused before reading. readCapped (l.180-198) counts the decoded bytes the reader yields, cancels the body past the cap, and copies into one resizable ArrayBuffer (9ee06e8: about the cap, not twice it; it grows past a too-small declared length, which closes the RangeError residual). sniffVideoType (l.201-205) types the clip from its bytes, so a non-video body is ledgered but not kept. The evidence records media.clip and media.frame origins. The comments (l.142-153) describe what is enforced. ADR-0088 records the media trust policy and extends ADR-0069. The two parked items were fixed later: renderer redirect hops (56e30ff, ADR-0096) and the asset re-buy (4b3f5b6).

findings.title: F18 — Enable a real browser-process containment boundary (byway-review.md:141 summary row, :339-347 body, :378 threat table, :427 order; produced by engine-protocol-review.md E9, :114-122)
findings.verdict: ACCEPT (both verifiers and both critics); severity kept at P2. Reframed: key custody is an extension of ADR-0030's 'keys never enter a sandbox', not a breach of spec §2 / ADR-0074 'Keys' (verification 3859, 4137).
findings.rootCause: launchChromium (pages.ts:241-243 at b33f128), the only production launch every renderer use passes through, stated no containment policy, so two defaults built for other contexts applied: Playwright's chromiumSandbox:false (adds --no-sandbox) and inheritance of process.env, which serve.ts had loaded with .env.agents' provider keys. The product described renderer containment only as in-browser controls (spec §3.2, ADR-0074) after ADR-0067 dropped ADR-0031's OS-isolated renderer without replacing it, and treated the renderer as a web-page renderer although BLIND-1 made it the shared renderer for every medium's lineup cards. No test checked effective flags or environment, and the lazy launch meant a renderer that cannot start was found only after paid steps (verification 3820-3834, 3865-3871).
findings.how: Both halves of the root cause were removed at the one launch boundary. chromiumLaunchOptions(setting, env) (packages/runner/src/pages.ts:315-316) is the only description of the launch: headless, chromiumSandbox from the person's setting, args exactly the two WebRTC flags, env = withoutSecrets(env, namesFromEnvFile(env)). launchChromium(setting) (pages.ts:2298-2306) is the only production launch, takes only the sandbox setting, calls Playwright once and maps any failure through launchFailure (pages.ts:348) with no retry and no fallback. The setting defaults on (RENDERER_OS_SANDBOX_DEFAULT = true; store's renderer_settings row, never set = on; an unreadable setting counts as on; serve.ts:191 also defaults on). Only Settings' PATCH /api/renderer writes it, and apps/web/test/guard-sandbox.test.ts pins every line that switches the setting, sets chromiumSandbox, builds a renderer or launches Chromium. A sandbox that cannot start gives per-OS why and fix (packages/runner/src/sandbox.ts), read from the whole error so Playwright's pipe-transport first line does not hide it; a drift test holds the words to the installed Playwright. Readiness reaches the sandboxed renderer process: ready() draws byway's own scripted test page (pages.ts:732-765); beginRun gates web-page runs (lifecycle.ts:28) and the model step gates runs with >=3 references including an image (model-step.ts:189-197, 890f88f); serve.ts prints a 'renderer' line and records it for Settings and the banner; scripts/e2e.ts:141-146 fails unless the line says 'inside its OS sandbox'. While the sandbox is off: confirmation, banner on every screen, a run note per step, the start-up line, and an offer to turn it back on. CI runs the whole gate on windows-2025 and ubuntu-24.04 (after scripts/linux/allow-chromium-sandbox.sh) with the sandbox on (run 39172144829 on the branch; main 8401820 run 39177268735 green). I confirmed in my clone that the targeted tests pass (launch, begin-run, sandbox, render-browsers, sandbox-note, gateway env, store renderer-settings, guard-sandbox: 104/104; renderer-check 21/21; the four real-Chromium pages.test.ts sandbox tests), and I ran five mutations, each caught: chromiumSandbox forced false (5 tests fail, including the CDP command-line test), env dropped from the options (2 fail), an unsandboxed retry inside launchChromium (6 fail), the beginRun gate removed (2 fail), and a stray chromium.launch in packages/runner/src (3 guard tests fail). One known exception to the env half stays open: the secrets-file names that do not look secret leak when the gateway's env module loads twice on a lowercase-drive Windows start (ADR-0100 item 6). Provider keys and secret-looking names still stay out, because those rules go by name.

findings.title: F19: Reject invalid Unicode in canonical object keys (byway-review.md:349-355; sub-review gateway-store-review.md GS-07, lines 29 and 99-103)
findings.severity: P3 (review P3). Lines 4180: the library breaks RFC 8785 and its own contract. Every path to the defect needs a lone surrogate, which can only arrive as a JSON \u escape.
findings.verdict: ACCEPT (verification line 46, 4176). Reproduced at b33f1285 by both verifiers and the designer's probes.
findings.rootCause: Lines 4171 and 4182. Well-formed text is a precondition of hashing (RFC 8785 for canonical JSON, UTF-8 for sha256Hex), but only canonical's string-value branch enforced it. Commit 54eed9e added the check there alone, so property names bypassed it, and sha256Hex silently hashed a lone surrogate as U+FFFD (a collision with the U+FFFD text). Deeper cause: none of the three places where untrusted text enters a hashed record made sure it was hashable. (1) parseRecipe returned recipes that recipeHash could not hash. (2) Ledger.verify assumed every parsed line was a hashable entry object. (3) ModelGateway.record copied provider-reported labels into the hash-chained entry after billing.

findings.title: F20 — A work cap must not substitute for human acceptance (byway-review.md lines 143, 357-365; engine-protocol-review.md E8)
findings.rootCause: Gate-exit policy has no single definition. The interpreter gives human-metric loops a private exit branch that treats exhaustion like approval and never reads the declared onCap. The shared atCap handler is reached only when a model critic or check reports straight to the loop. Which critic feeds a gate is undecided: the validator's containsCritic walks through every container, while the interpreter drops the loop context at replicate, each, audit and gate. LS1 checks a declared onCap that one branch, and every feedless critic loop, ignore. Spec, protocol, estimator, catalog comment and validator each state a different exit policy (line 233).
findings.how: The private human-loop exit is gone. Every way a loop reaches its cap goes through Interpreter.capTurn (interpreter.ts:679-696): after a critic or check (atCap), at the last round of a person's loop (interpreter.ts:579-584, in place of the last 'Is this ready?'), and after a round that ran to its end with no verdict (:590-594). With onCap human, a person's loop asks 'That was the last planned round. Use this version? No allows up to N more rounds, once.' with the work and the round's notes beside it. No raises the cap once, and at the raised cap a 'choose' asks 'Use this version' or 'Stop the run' (RunStopped, which ends the run cancelled). Admission keeps the policy reachable: LS1 refuses a person's loop whose cap goes to a policy, ST2/ST10 'feed' refuse a critic or check loop or gate whose critic does not report on every round (gateFeed in the shared semantics), and ST10 'metric' refuses one-shot check-clean and human gates. The estimator (planned) and workBound (withRaise) read one loopRounds, and the C2/C6a copy says more rounds can be allowed once. Unit tests drive the real Interpreter to the cap, an e2e drives C6a's author loop through the real workflow, and semantics-exits holds the feed and exit semantics to the interpreter.

findings.title: Make verification repeatable in CI (release action 1)
findings.rootCause: Verification exists only as documented local commands, and nothing runs them on change, so every 'CI check' the spec and the ADRs rely on is enforced from memory. The commands' prerequisites (Node, pnpm, runner OS, Chromium for the unit suite, the Temporal CLI) are written as minimums or manual steps, not provisioned, pinned inputs (verification:4414).
findings.how: The cause is removed for main. .github/workflows/verify.yml runs `pnpm verify` (typecheck && vitest && e2e) on windows-2025 and ubuntu-24.04 on every push to main, by hand and weekly. It checks out the whole history, uses a read-only token and no secrets. Node is pinned in .node-version (24.13.1), pnpm in packageManager (pnpm@11.28.6), every action by commit SHA and runner images by explicit label. Chromium (with --with-deps on Linux) and the Temporal CLI are provisioned before the tests. Linux also needs an AppArmor profile and Noto CJK; no product code needed changing (ADR-0103 §3). scripts/test/ci.test.ts holds the workflow to this shape, so deleting it, changing its triggers or unpinning it fails `pnpm verify`. ADR-0103 §5-§6 restate what 'CI' means in CR14, ADR-0055, ADR-0059, the spec and ADR-0068's merge gate. The 'Protect main' and 'Protect tags' rulesets block force pushes and deletions; I read them as active with a read-only `gh api` call. CI blocks nothing: it reports after a push, and branches run CI only when dispatched by hand. A required check waits for a filed trigger. CI is green on main at 8401820 (run 39177268735). Main run 39079760987 went red, so the gate does fail.

findings.title: Keep a compact current-decision index (release action 3)
findings.rootCause: The ADR log has a rule for replacing decisions (write a new ADR) but no structured, checked relation between a record and the records that change it. It also had no rule for finalising a Proposed record's Decision on acceptance, and CR14's append-only check was not implemented. So corrections land only in the new record, old text keeps reading as current, prose relation verbs are optional and inconsistent, and hand-maintained summaries carry no link to their source (verification:4462).
findings.how: Built: ADR-0103 §1 (Context and Decision final once on main's first-parent history as Accepted; --no-ff merges; the accepting commit may finalise; from ADR-0103 on, the 'changed by' link lands in the same commit) and §2. scripts/test/adr-records.test.ts with adr-log.ts runs in pnpm verify and in CI. It fails an edit to, or the removal of, an Accepted record's Context or Decision after it reached main; an Accepted Decision that opens 'Proposed'; an index status that differs from the header; a 'changed by' link to a missing or later record or one not reciprocated; a record with no index row; and, from ADR-0103 on, a late link. Its temp-repo cases prove the rule. ADR-0041 gets a non-ratification note in ADR-0103 §7. f230909 back-filled the index 'changed by' links, so 0071, 0072, 0074, 0079 and 0066 all point to the records that change them. Root README's stale range became a link (f6e4ca9), and readme.test.ts forbids such a range. Not built: the verification's named root cause, a structured and checked relation, is only partly removed. The links are hand-added to the index, and the check 'cannot see a missing "changed by" link' (ADR-0103 §2). A future record that corrects an old one without adding the link passes, which is how 0077 and 0079 drifted. The history-table Outcome pointers are not done.

findings.title: Define a local backup/recovery acceptance scenario (release action 4)
findings.rootCause: Authoritative state is split across independently written stores: SQLite in WAL mode, CAS files referenced from SQLite, a JSONL ledger with its .head, the exposure register, and Temporal's SQLite. Nothing defines which set of files, in which state, is a backup. The one written statement was wrong and never exercised. Start-up reconciliation covers only the store-ahead-of-Temporal direction, and the ledger treats a missing file as zero spend (verification:4482).
findings.how: Each part of the cause is addressed. ADR-0094 defines the backup unit: every file in BYWAY_DATA_DIR, copied with byway stopped and the engine confirmed gone (port and process check). A restore replaces the whole directory. This corrects ADR-0066, and the index links them. The README 'Back up and restore' section gives Windows and Linux commands and names what each mix does. scripts/test/backup.test.ts shows that a single-file copy taken while the store is open lacks committed data, and that a whole-directory copy reopens intact. It also requires the README to name every file byway writes. ADR-0096 adds checkStore (quick_check, missing or wrong-size artifact files with the runs that use them) and dataDirReport, printed at start before the engine. It also makes reconcileLostRuns a two-way pass that terminates orphan run workflows with ORPHAN_RUN_MESSAGE before the worker polls. F03's spend book in byway.sqlite (ADR-0095 decision 9) took cap authority away from the JSONL ledger, so a lost or older ledger no longer resets the caps. The two F03 restore stubs became plain tests (082bebe), and the README caveat was removed with that fail-open (ADR-0100 item 15). The split stores remain by design; the likely bad mixes are now detected or made harmless. The engine-ahead-of-store-on-the-same-run mix remains undetected, as a recorded limit.

findings.title: Retain accessibility work and test the interactive boundaries (release action 5)
findings.rootCause: Accessibility is built into components as static attributes, and nothing exercises state transitions in a real browser with the keyboard. 'An action in flight' has no shared owner: each component implements busy and unavailable states on its own, mostly by handing both focus behaviour and double-submit protection to the DOM `disabled` attribute. So RunScreen's correct aria-disabled-plus-guard pattern was not reused, and nothing stops `disabled` from coming back (verification:4507).
findings.how: Action-in-flight state now has one shared owner, apps/web/src/components/useAction.ts plus ActionButton.tsx. A synchronous guard refuses a second start before React re-renders, and controls stay focusable with aria-disabled and aria-busy. Every self-disabling or busy control is converted: the panels, SelectPanel's bulk buttons, Start, the paid Start, Build my own and the Examples file input. guard-disabled.test.ts fails any native `disabled` in apps/web src/ and app/ outside three reviewed entries (Examples fieldset, 'Paste an example', Switch), and fails a stale entry. The rule is written in the apps/web README Guardrails. RunScreen returns focus to the timeline row that opened a step. e2e/keyboard.spec.ts drives these transitions with the keyboard in a real browser, through pnpm e2e and CI. The cross-cluster stubs for F05, F06, F07 and F13 became plain tests once those fixes landed. Beyond the verification's 'no server idempotency' choice, ADR-0099 decision 7 later added run-start idempotency on the server. The final-check residual about a blocked Start is closed: RecommendationView start() returns when blocked (:391), and ActionButton has unavailable={blocked} (:514).

review.verdict:
Nothing in the review is left without a disposition on main. But the claim that every item is resolved does not hold yet, for three reasons: two acceptance items in F01 and F02 are still open, about 35 residuals are filed with no trigger, and the fix status page is wrong in places.

**Coverage.** The inventory says it has 247 items, but its list has 312: 153 under F, 17 under R, 2 under RS, 70 X-items and 70 sub-review items.
- **F, R and RS items (172):** all map to the per-cluster traces.
- **The other 140, traced here:**
  - 100 are addressed on main, either by the F fixes or by research-track records that predate the review.
  - 17 are filed with a trigger. Most of these are harness requirements behind the 'Before the study registry's first entry' row, which label.test.ts trips.
  - 7 are filed with no trigger.
  - 11 are recorded as research-track scope.
  - 5 are unaddressed: dependency or security scanning (X-VAL-3, X-VAL-5, X-COV-2), the protocol map's Google Fonts (SUB-DA-8), and cancelling a large fan-out (SUB-DA-4).
- **Two inventory 'none found' entries are wrong.** F03.15 and F03.18 are addressed by ADR-0099 decision 7: a Start id stands for one Start, and reusing it with other inputs returns 409.

**Substance.**
- **The three P1 guarantees are closed on main with tests:** VOICE protection (ADR-0092 plus the run-time guard), drafts (ADR-0082) and exact copy (ADR-0081).
- **No traced finding is symptom-only, except F03's minor UI sub-cause:** the paid call during the GET render.
- **Two root fixes are incomplete:**
  - F01: the audit, gate and each port semantics are still defined twice, with no executed agreement test (G01).
  - F02: run inputs are still carried by value, and that row has no trigger (G04).

**Record-keeping.**
- **The status page's 'What remains: —' is untrue for 14 rows.** It also miscites ADR-0094 for R1 and RS, and undercounts F01's owner questions (G06).
- **ADR index links are missing, and R3's own trigger has fired unacted (G07).**
- **Decision evidence that Accepted ADRs rely on lives only in %TEMP%, under a trigger nobody can observe (G03).**
- **About ten rows wait on a 'first live run' that has no trigger, and live C5 is gated on rows with no trigger, which is circular (G05).**

**What to do first.** None of this is high severity, so the work is closing the record rather than re-fixing defects:
1. Correct the status page and the ADR links.
2. Copy the Temp evidence into the repository now.
3. Add the F01 operator-agreement test and the keepsVoice activity-level test.
4. Give the untriggered rows observable triggers.
5. File G02, which matters for the planned Claude Code channel because it would add a new caller of Runner.start.
